title: Key Information Document before agreeing terms with an agency worker (employment businesses)
summary: Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003, regulation 13A: an employment business must give every new work-seeker a Key Information Document before agreeing terms with them. It covers the type of contract, the minimum expected rate of pay, who pays them, deductions and fees, an example of take-home pay, and holiday entitlement and pay. GOV.UK publishes templates for PAYE, umbrella-company and personal-service-company workers. Since 7 April 2026 the Fair Work Agency enforces it in place of the Employment Agency Standards Inspectorate. It does not apply in Northern Ireland.

title: PAYE in labour supply chains that include umbrella companies (joint and several liability)
summary: Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003, Part 2 Chapter 11: for payments made on or after 6 April 2026, where an umbrella company employs a worker, the agency that contracts with the end client (or the end client, if there is no agency) is jointly and severally liable for PAYE income tax and Class 1 National Insurance the umbrella company fails to pay. Due diligence is not a defence. This is separate from the planned employment-agency regulation of umbrella companies under the Employment Rights Act 2025.

title: Pay-between-assignments contracts ("Swedish derogation") still permitted in Northern Ireland
summary: Agency Workers Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2011, regulation 10: an agency worker employed on a permanent contract and paid between assignments may lose the right to equal pay after the 12-week qualifying period, if the strict contract and payment conditions are met. Great Britain abolished this on 6 April 2020. The Northern Ireland Good Jobs Employment Rights Bill proposes abolishing it and introducing a Key Information Document, but neither is law yet.
